sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid_Bijural - Quebec private law, including partnerships, is governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (Code civil du Quebec); federal and provincial public law, criminal law and taxation follow the common law tradition. French is the official language of commerce and of the enterprise registry.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force 1 July 2020
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union, provisionally applied since 21 September 2017
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force 30 December 2018
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force 1 October 2014
Canada-Hong Kong FIPA, in force 6 September 2016
Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement, in force 1 January 2015
Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement, in force 5 July 1997

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Quebec: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2186-2251 (societe en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1) and Regulation (CQLR c P-44.1, r 1); Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 and Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal - the Registraire des entreprises publishes only the identity of the general partner(s) (commandites) of a Quebec limited partnership; limited partners' beneficial ownership schedule is not registered publicly and remains internal to the LP, subject to lawful access by Revenu Quebec, FINTRAC and courts under production orders.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Contrat de societe en commandite (Limited Partnership Agreement) - executed original or certified copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or licensed legal counsel in the partner's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing jurisdiction (Canada has been a Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention since 11 January 2024); consular legalization only for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / incumbency certificate of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or company registrar of the general partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (if issued outside Canada)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) appointing the Quebec resident attorney-in-fact and/or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; if executed in Quebec, notarized before a Quebec notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO identification file: passport copies, proof of residential address and source of funds declarations for every ultimate beneficial owner at or above 25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commissioner of oaths / notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for cross-border use; domestic notarization sufficient if the UBO is resident in Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and quarterly refresh screening of all partners, directors and UBOs against: (i) Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists under SEMA, the United Nations Act and the Magnitsky Law; (ii) Public Safety Canada and FINTRAC advisories/indicators; (iii) the US OFAC SDN List (given USD payment rails); (iv) the UN Security Council consolidated list. Any PEP or head of international organization match requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds evidence and escalation to senior management. For this Low_Risk_Standard subscription-commerce LP, the payment processors (Stripe Billing, Authorize.Net) independently perform KYB/KYC and cardholder screening, but the LP remains responsible for identifying its own non-resident limited partners at the 25% beneficial-ownership threshold.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) - online portal: registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; name reservation via the online module 'Rechercher et reserver un nom'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory French legal name: pursuant to the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and P-44.1, the registered name must be in French unless the Registrar accepts a recognized trademark or the s. 21 exemption. English ('Limited Partnership') is permitted only as a complement to the French designation 'societe en commandite' (abbreviation 'S.E.C.' or 'SEC'). Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Roman characters and translated into French for the registry record.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Bancaire (requires federal OSFI or AMF approval)
Trust / Fiducie / Fiduciary (requires AMF or federal letters patent)
Avocat / Barreau / Lawyer / Attorney (reserved to members of the Barreau du Quebec)
Notaire / Notary (reserved to members of the Chambre des notaires du Quebec)
Universite / University / College / Institut (requires Ministry of Higher Education authorization if implying an educational institution)
Commission / Conseil / Council / Police (implies a public or governmental body; requires ministerial clearance)
Royal / Royale / Reine / Queen / Crown (requires Crown authorization)
Canada / Canadian / Canadien (where the name falsely suggests a federal or governmental authority)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a request for reconsideration (demande de revision) with the Registraire des entreprises within 10 days of the rejection notice, invoking s. 17 of P-44.1 and ss. 13-15 of the Regulation (CQLR c P-44.1, r 1). If the reconsideration is denied, appeal lies to the Tribunal administratif du Quebec within 30 days of the decision. Counsel should file two or three alternative names in the same session to avoid delay; where the Registrar's practice permits, an existing reservation may be renewed before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted - Quebec law (P-44.1 and Civil Code of Quebec art. 2238) requires the LP to designate a real 'etablissement' / 'siege' in Quebec at which legal documents may be served and books may be examined. A non-PO-Box street address supplied by a licensed virtual-office/registered-agent provider satisfies the requirement; a mail-forwarding-only arrangement without any physical presence in Quebec may be rejected by the Registrar and would expose the LP to deregistration for lack of commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 5% or less annual probability for a standard e-commerce subscription-box enterprise. Unannounced inspections are not a routine practice of the Registraire des entreprises; they may occur if triggered by a Revenu Quebec tax audit, a FINTRAC AML inquiry, or a consumer-protection complaint. The LP should retain the virtual-office agreement, warehouse/fulfilment contracts and bank/payment-processor statements to evidence commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation at the Registraire des entreprises (one application)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff approximately CAD 40 (s. 4 of the Regulation respecting fees under P-44.1)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration (immatriculation) of the societe en commandite / limited partnership
NUANS trademark/collision search report (optional but recommended)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ), arts. 2186–2260, in particular arts. 2236–2260 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1, arts. 1–3, 10–35 and 51–62; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (c. P-44.1, r. 1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar, REQ), an administrative body attached to the Ministère de la Justice du Québec.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation — Société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed in the Quebec enterprise register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Quebec limited partnership. Contributions may consist of money, property or rights (CCQ arts. 2253–2254) but a limited partner (commanditaire) may not contribute labour or services; all contributions must be recorded in the partnership register. No escrow account is statutorily mandated; subscription prepayments are deferred revenue held in an operating account at a Canadian Schedule I bank or through PCI-DSS-compliant merchant settlement accounts (Stripe Billing / Authorize.Net), subject to the Quebec Consumer Protection Act prohibitions on false or unconscionable representations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, NUANS Report and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online 'Recherche de nom / Réservation de nom' module at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary availability search in the Quebec enterprise register; generate a NUANS real-time report either through the REQ's online search tool or an accredited NUANS agent; submit a name reservation application listing up to three ranked candidate names, each including the mandatory designator 'Société en commandite', 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'; collect the reservation notice and attach it to the subsequent declaration of registration.
required_dossiers: NUANS real-time report dated within 90 days
Name reservation application with three ranked candidate names
Mandate or power of attorney if filed through a third-party agent
Identification of the general partner(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, re-file with a new distinctive element or obtain a written consent/disclaimer from the prior registrant; a formal name re-examination may be requested from the REQ; any refusal is fully curable before the declaration of registration is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Partnership Agreement (Convention de Société en Commandite) and Drafting of the Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Barreau du Québec / Chambre des notaires du Québec legal counsel; no government filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement governing capital contributions (CCQ art. 2253), distribution waterfall, the general partner's exclusive management powers, transfer restrictions for limited partner interests, indemnification, dissolution and Quebec governing law; verify the prohibition against limited partners performing services for the partnership; if the general partner is a legal person, obtain its constating documents and resolution authorizing the partnership; prepare the REQ declaration of registration for signature by the general partners.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement executed by all partners
Capital contribution schedule with valuations of in-kind contributions
Constating documents or certificate of existence of a corporate general partner
Identification and domicile of every limited partner
Confirmation of the Quebec registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration contains gaps, execute a supplementary amending act before filing; if a limited partner is a foreign entity, obtain a capacity legal opinion; cure any mismatch between the partnership agreement and the intended register data prior to submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration and Payment of Fees (REQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — electronic filing service ('Déclaration d'immatriculation'), or in-person service counters in Québec City, Montréal and Gatineau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and transmit the declaration of registration online; attach the NUANS report and the duly signed declaration together with true copies of partner identification; pay the official filing fee (approximately CAD 45, shown as USD 33 in the budget); upon acceptance, obtain the electronic acknowledgement containing the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ); download the official certificate of immatriculation from the REQ portal.
required_dossiers: Declaration of registration (REQ form or accepted data schema) signed by general partners
Valid NUANS report attached to the declaration
Payment of the official state filing fee
Copy of the name reservation notice, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If processing is interrupted for missing attachments, cure within the REQ's 30-day query window; if the application is refused, amend the conflicting fields and refile; a statutory revision request may be submitted to the REQ, with final judicial remedy available before the civil courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Publicity, Certificate Collection and Third-Party Opposability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (register publication and certificate issuance; no separate gazette step for partnerships)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the public file displays the partnership's legal publicity date and that the disclosed data (name, partnership domicile, general partners, objectives) is complete; obtain the official certificate of registration as evidence of existence and of the limited liability opposability of the commanditaires toward third parties; service all subsequent amendments on the REQ within 30 days.
required_dossiers: REQ certificate of immatriculation issued after registration
Partnership agreement for governance records
Partner list and capital schedule stored at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate reflects an error, use the REQ rectification procedure under sections 51 and following of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; if the register reveals a lapse, file a declaration of resumption of activity before effecting any transaction with third parties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Quebec Tax Account Registration (BN, GST/HST, TVQ and Payroll)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec — Quebec Business Number and TVQ/QST account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number with programs RM (GST/HST) and RT (payroll) through CRA Business Registration Online; simultaneously activate the Quebec TVQ/QST account at Revenu Québec using the NEQ as the identifier; note the mandatory registration threshold of CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies; the partnership files annual information returns (T5013 and Quebec Relevé 10) while partners report their shares in their own returns; set up payment rails using Stripe Billing or Authorize.Net merchant accounts.
required_dossiers: NEQ certificate and REQ registration data
Partnership agreement indicating shares, capital and management powers
Identification or SIN/BN of the general partners
Estimated annual revenue declaration
Bank account details for direct deposit and merchant settlement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If account activation is delayed, present the NEQ certificate and REQ extract to CRA or Revenu Québec to expedite; request a retroactive effective date if registration occurred after the first taxable supply; for non-resident partners, consider the deemed resident election under CRA form RC459.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Records, Registered Office Setup and Signature Delegation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner and partnership counsel or notary; no government filing beyond REQ record updates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the registered office at the declared Quebec address; create a partners' register recording all capital contributions, transfers and withdrawals; institutionalize the governance organs (general partner with management authority; appointed managers as signatories); file any change of address or officer data with the REQ within 30 days; keep the pro-forma organizational resolution in the minute book; execute bank mandates and authorize payment gateway operations.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma organizational resolution / partners' written consent
Partners' register and capital schedule
Lease or letter of authorization for the registered office address
Specimen signatures and copies of manager identities
Bank account and payment gateway mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank refuses account opening, provide the REQ certificate and the organizational resolution; if governance disputes arise, the partnership agreement prevails and a notarized amending declaration can clarify signature powers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal permits authority — Ville de Montréal, Service des permis et consultations, or the applicable local municipality where the fulfillment center is located; no provincial industrial manufacturing board applies to subscription-box retail under ISIC 4791.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Establishment Permit (Permis d'exploitation commerciale) for warehousing and small-package distribution, together with a Fire Safety Compliance Certificate for the premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Direction régionale de l'inspection
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Low-risk registration / conditionally exempt tier — no mandatory full EIA because the activity is a retail distribution warehouse without industrial processes; a declaration of activities under the Environment Quality Act (LQE, c. Q-2) may be required only where packaging waste exceeds municipal thresholds, contaminated soil is encountered, or refrigeration systems contain HFCs at or above 1,000 kg.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge by-laws and the Water Withdrawal and Protection Regulation (RPEP); combustion and forklift emissions must remain below the Clean Air Regulation exhaust concentration limits (general VOC ceiling of 80 mg/m³ and NOx ceiling of 130 mg/m³ dry stack where applicable); packaging waste must be diverted in accordance with RECYC-QUÉBEC extended producer responsibility regulations, with a target diversion rate above 75% for cardboard and mixed recyclables.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (attestation de conformité en sécurité incendie) issued by the municipal fire prevention service covering egress, storage of combustible cardboard in compliance with NFPA 13 sprinkler requirements, emergency lighting and signage; structural load clearance for racking and aisle configurations certified by an engineer under the Building Act; mandatory employer registration with the CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) and adoption of a workplace health and safety program for loading docks and mechanical handling equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal GST/HST and Income Tax Act administration; Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST), provincial income tax and the Quebec enterprise registry. Portals: CRA Business Registration Online, CRA My Business Account, Canada Business Network, and Revenu Québec Cl@rassant.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned limited partnership must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and the relevant program accounts through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1. Quebec registration is integrated through Revenu Québec's Form LM-1 and the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec), which also creates the QST account. The partnership, not the general partner, is the registrant for GST/QST and files the applicable information returns. A non-resident LP must designate a Canadian representative for service of process, provide the partnership agreement and the Quebec limited partnership registration extract (société en commandite), and open any required payroll or import/export accounts depending on operational footprint.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime. A limited partnership is fiscally transparent; income is computed at the entity level for allocation to partners. Relevant elections include: (i) the Income Tax Act s. 96(2.1) election, filed with Form T5013/T5013SUM, allowing a non-resident partner's allocable share of Canadian partnership income to be taxed under Part I as Canadian business income instead of triggering gross-basis Part XIII withholding on distributions; (ii) the Excise Tax Act s. 273 partnership election to treat certain supplies as made by partners for GST/HST; and (iii) the corresponding Revenu Québec QST elections.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_note: Pass-through applies for income tax purposes, but for GST/HST and QST the partnership is itself a 'person' required to carry its own registration and collect and remit tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual consumption tax regime: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5%, combined with Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.5%, producing a combined headline rate of 14.5% in Quebec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148 and the aligned QST small-supplier rule. Registration is compulsory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, tested on total taxable supplies made in Canada and elsewhere; voluntary registration is available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance regime, no CRA or Revenu Québec API-based invoice validation, and no digital stamping requirement. Invoices must contain prescribed content, including the supplier's GST/HST and QST registration numbers, date, description of the subscription box goods, and tax charged. Pan-Canadian PEPPOL BIS 3.0 e-invoicing is mandatory only for transactions with federal procurers; private-sector B2B e-invoicing in Quebec is governed by commercial agreement rather than tax clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The LP may zero-rate subscription-box goods sold to non-residents provided the tangible personal property is exported from Canada and delivered outside Canada, satisfying Schedule VI, Part V of the ETA (notably s. 1(e) and s. 1(f)) and the corresponding QST provisions. Recurring subscriber services supplied to non-resident customers may also be zero-rated where the services are not substantially performed in Canada and the recipient is outside Canada. Zero-rating is conditional on obtaining and preserving contemporaneous evidence of export, destination, and payment. Canada imposes no statutory outward-remittance deadline; the 180-day figure stated below is an internal repatriation and evidence-matching benchmark for subscription-export collections.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration (Form A15414 or carrier-filed Electronic Export Report) filed within 15 days after export
Commercial invoice with HS classification for the subscription box contents, Incoterms, and declaration of Canada as country of origin
Transport document evidencing delivery outside Canada: Bill of Lading, sea or air waybill, or international parcel carrier record (Canada Post/USPS/FedEx/DHL)

Payment settlement evidence from Stripe Billing or Authorize.Net, including card-settlement reports, SWIFT confirmations, or bank/FX conversion receipts, functionally equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess a zero-rated claim within four years of the original assessment, extended to seven years for misrepresentation arising from neglect, carelessness, or omission, and without limitation in cases of willful fraud. False or misleading statements supporting an export zero-rating claim attract the Excise Tax Act s. 285 penalty of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the overstated refund or net tax, plus interest under s. 280, and the corresponding QST penalty framework. Deliberate or grossly negligent conduct can also trigger the 50% gross-negligence penalty, criminal prosecution under tax evasion provisions, full clawback of the refund, and denial of future export zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility for both capital and current account transactions. No foreign exchange controls restrict the repatriation of dividends, partnership distributions, or loan repayments. The CAD floats freely; cross-border funds movements are subject to anti-money laundering reporting thresholds under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), not exchange-control permits. Non-resident partners may remit profits without prior government approval, but banks impose standard source-of-funds and tax compliance documentation requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds in Canada. Exporters may hold foreign currency balances in Canadian or offshore bank accounts without conversion obligations. However, under the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC regulations, a financial institution must prepare a large cash transaction report for cash payments of CAD 10,000 or more; international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more require reporting by the bank to FINTRAC. No statutory timeline requires conversion of export receipts into CAD.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Foreign digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Transferroom) may provide cross-border payment services to a Canadian-domiciled LP if the EMI holds a public money services business (MSB) registration under FINTRAC or operates under a permissible exemption. These EMIs are not licensed as Canadian deposit-taking institutions and therefore cannot offer CDIC-insured CAD accounts, issue Canadian bank clearing/routing numbers, or provide settlement through the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS)/Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) directly. Legal constraints include the need to deposit client funds in trust at a Canadian bank, compliance with final payment and sanctions screening, and inability to hold or disburse funds as a substitute for a term operating bank account. For recurring subscription box cash flows, EMIs should be used only as supplementary disbursement conduits, not as the primary treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video-onboarding is accepted by most Tier-1 Canadian banks for directors who are Canadian residents. For non-resident directors or individuals exercising control over the LP, enhanced due diligence often requires an in-person interview at the bank branch, or a certified true copy of passport and proof of address with apostille/notarisation, plus a banker's reference from the home jurisdiction. Canadian banks may require the general partner of the LP to appear physically if the LP has any non-resident limited partners. A full in-person board appearance is typically mandated if a corporate general partner or another partnership is in the control chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership structure with non-resident limited partners and no imposed minimum capital reserve.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed partnership agreement, certified register of limited partners, declarations of beneficial ownership (UBO form), professional source-of-wealth statements from non-resident partners, notarised constitutional documents, and a bank reference letter covering the general partner's financial history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Subscription box model processed through payment aggregators (Stripe, Authorize.Net) generating recurring cross-border internet flows and possible merchant-credit risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial business plan with historical transaction summaries, payment processor settlement reports, fulfilment warehouse lease or logistics agreement, chargeback management policy, and a detailed data-protection / PCI-DSS compliance certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners behind a cascade of shell holding entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Entity chart depicting all layers up to ultimate natural persons, corporate registry extracts for all intermediate entities, certified board resolutions, and a valid Revenu Québec LP registration certificate proving substance in Quebec.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound trade disbursements to suppliers in high- or medium-risk jurisdictions for subscription box inventory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supplier contracts, customs import and warehouse documents, invoice/packing lists for underlying goods, shipping and tracking evidence, and a copy of the company's internal KYC and sanctions-screen procedure covering each vendor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections should be executed via SWIFT MT103 (international credit transfer) from the non-resident partner's bank to the LP's Canadian operating account. Remittance instructions must include a descriptive narrative such as 'Capital contribution to Quebec limited partnership for subscription box business.' The bank will require the exact LP legal name, bank BIC/SWIFT code, and domestic account/routing number (institution + transits). If the transfer amount exceeds CAD 10,000, the receiving bank reports the details to FINTRAC. There is no need for a surrender certificate or government exchange-control permit; however, the LP's KYC file must already include the source of funds and the partnership structure before any inbound credit is booked.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for international inventory and logistics vendors should be routed primarily over the SWIFT network using MT103 messages, typically in the vendor's invoiced currency or CAD under a spot conversion. For high-value or recurring production purchases, banks may issue commercial letters of credit (clause of UCP 600) with applicable safeguards. Domestic disbursements (e.g., Quebec warehouse leases, carrier invoices) clear via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or through ACSS electronic debit. Bulk and recurring payments can use DTCC or pre-authorized debits; all outbound wire instructions must be pre-validated against bank sanctions lists and the LP's KYC internal procedures. For USD payments, the LP may utilise a USD clearing USD account maintained at the same Canadian bank or a correspondent U.S. bank; otherwise, banks convert internally at a pre-agreed desk rate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forward contracts for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and other liquid trade currencies up to typical 12-month tenors.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging market currencies (e.g., RMB, MXN) where offshore deliverable forwards are unavailable or illiquid.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term USD funding or structural trade payables driven by recurring subscription box imports.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual enterprise declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the enterprise's REQ-assigned 'annual date' (anniversary of original registration month); amending declaration due within 30 days of any change to registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs an administrative monetary penalty; repeated non-filing triggers a registrar cancellation notice and administrative strike-off (radiation) of the limited partnership's registration, potentially compromising the limited liability shield of limited partners until revival is completed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary, T5013 member slips, financial statements) and Schedule 50 if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end; for a December 31 fiscal period end, no later than May 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500), additional penalties for failure to provide information, and criminal sanctions for willful default; un filed returns may also result in disallowance of partnership expense claims

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec partnership information return (TP-600 Société de personnes declaration and partner schedules, including CO-437 slips as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the federal T5013; for a fiscal period ending December 31, generally due no later than May 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalties under the Taxation Act (Québec), including CAD 25 per day capped at CAD 2,500, plus potential reassessment of partners and refusal to recognize partnership allocations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit threshold for a private Québec société en commandite; an audit is compulsory only if required by the partnership agreement, a creditor or investor covenant, or if the LP becomes a reporting issuer under securities legislation (not applicable to a low-risk subscription box LP); a review engagement of annual financial statements normally satisfies commercial practice
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private entities; partnership income is computed under the federal Income Tax Act and the Québec Taxation Act

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Québec and Canada do not impose a standalone annual UBO registry filing on a non-reporting limited partnership; the REQ annual declaration serves as the annual confirmation of registered partners and general partner/management particulars. Any transfer of partnership interests, admission or withdrawal of partners, or change in place of business must be recorded in internal registers and a REQ amending declaration filed within 30 days of the event. FINTRAC AML obligations require the LP to maintain beneficial ownership information internally, but no separate annual beneficial-ownership filing is triggered for this entity.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (registre des associés, including limited partners)
Register of General Partners (registre des commandités)
Minute Book (livre de procès-verbaux) containing resolutions of general partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220 – USD 590 per annum (CAD 300 – CAD 800; typical Québec registered office and corporate agent service fee for a private limited partnership)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,200 – USD 11,100 per annum (CAD 3,000 – CAD 15,000; typical review or audit engagement fee for a small subscription-box limited partnership)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at LP entity level (fiscally transparent); corporate partners are subject to combined federal and Quebec corporate rate of 26.5% (15% federal + 11.5% Quebec) on allocated taxable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: LP itself claims no corporate deductions or credits; eligible business losses and tax credits (e.g., Quebec innovation tax credit, federal SR&ED) flow through to partners at their applicable rates

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (and related T5013 Summary) filed electronically using CRA's T5013 Web Forms, commercial tax software, or Internet File Transfer
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before March 31 immediately following the calendar year in which the partnership's fiscal period ends (e.g., fiscal year ending December 31, 2024 is due March 31, 2025)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership identification and province of establishment; indicates that the entity is a Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicates whether the partnership has non-resident partners; no additional identification required beyond legal name and business number

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income (loss) of the partnership from all active commercial activities, including recurring subscription box sales classified under NAICS 454110 and ISIC 4791
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate to non-resident partners only their share of income that is attributable to Canadian sources; for treaty purposes, business income of a non-resident partner is exempt unless attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rental income (loss), if the LP owns or leases physical premises for subscription box warehousing or packing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must report Canadian-source rental income separately; consider submitting Form NR6 or a section 216 election if net rental income is sought

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital gains (losses) from disposition of Canadian taxable property, e.g., sale of a subscription box warehouse or shares in a Canadian company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are taxable on gains from disposition of taxable Canadian property; the partnership must withhold under Part XIII if it pays proceeds to a non-resident at the end of the year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) of the partnership for the fiscal period; agrees to the sum of allocated shares reported on partners' T5013 slips
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount forms the base for each partner's Canadian filing; non-residents may need to file a T1 or T2 return to report their allocated share if tax is payable or a refund is claimed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's name, address, and allocated share of income/loss for the period; must match the partnership agreement and reconcile to Box 32
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate strictly under the partnership agreement; provide Form NR301 where treaty relief is claimed; ensure the non-resident partner's share is not reported as a dividend

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: $25 per day per partner, minimum $100, maximum $2,500 for a fiscal period (increased to $7,500 for partnerships with more than 20 partners); gross negligence or intentional failure may attract an additional 50% penalty on tax evaded plus criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provincial/Quebec: TP-600 – Déclaration de revenus d'une société de personnes (Revenu Québec), filed electronically through Revenu Québec's e-services, commercial software, or service provider
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the last day of the month following the fiscal period end; for a December 31 year-end, the deadline is March 31 of the following year (aligned with federal T5013)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise registration number (NEQ), legal form, and fiscal period dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify whether the LP is an unincorporated registered partnership (immatriculation) with any extra-provincial or foreign partners

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec-source business income from subscription box sales delivered to Quebec customers, including online sales taxed from a Quebec establishment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenu Québec generally follows the federal allocation; non-residents are liable for Quebec tax only if the LP carries on business through a Quebec establishment or the income is allocated to a Quebec PE of the partner

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (loss) of the partnership after allocation of all income to partners; must match totals of the federal T5013 where no specific provincial adjustments apply
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use this amount to file a Quebec TP-1 (for individuals) or TP-3 (for corporations) in accordance with the partner's status; treaty relief is claimed using Form NR301-D

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner-by-partner allocation schedule of income/loss and tax credit claims (e.g., SR&ED credits) passed through to the partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must provide a Quebec certificate of residence or a copy of their foreign tax authority certificate to claim exemption or reduced tax under a DTA

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec imposes a late-filing penalty of $25 per day per partner, minimum $100, maximum $2,500; false or incomplete declarations expose the partnership to a 50% civil penalty and, in case of omission, to a penalty equal to the greater of $500 or 5% of the unreported amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Canadian Part XIII withholding tax on dividends and deemed dividends paid by a Canadian corporation; not typically applied to LP distributions as an LP is fiscally transparent – non-resident partners are instead subject to Part I tax on their allocated Canadian-source business income, with no separate dividend withholding at the partnership level)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief on any Part XIII amount (e.g., Canadian-source interest or royalties paid by the LP, or a corporate partner's dividend), the non-resident beneficial owner must complete and provide CRA Form NR301 (or NR301-S) and submit an official Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority; the Canadian payer/agent may reduce or exempt the withholding if satisfied that the recipient is a resident of a treaty jurisdiction and the reduced rate is applicable. For LP business income, a non-resident partner generally files a Canadian tax return and invokes the relevant business-property article of the applicable DTA, typically in the Canada-United States convention or another bilateral treaty, proving the absence of a Canadian permanent establishment where exemption is sought.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% under Part XIII, reduced by most Canadian DTAs to 0% (e.g., Canada-United States royalty withholding eliminated for most IP under the Fifth Protocol) or occasionally 10-15% for specific industrial royalties. Interest: statutory 25% Part XIII; arm's-length interest paid to non-resident arm's length beneficiaries is generally exempt from Canadian withholding tax unless payment is profit-participating or excessive; under the Canada-US treaty, interest is generally exempt at 0% for arm's-length recipients, and 15% for related-party contingent interest. Quebec does not levy a separate dividend or cross-border royalty withholding tax; the single federal rate applies, although Quebec imposes an additional tax on certain payments to non-residents under the Tax Administration Act for services rendered in Quebec.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate annual value of transactions with non-resident related parties triggers mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (and filing of T106 information return) for taxpayers with gross revenue under CAD 50,000,000; for larger taxpayers, any related-party cross-border transaction above a threshold of CAD 5,000,000 requires full Master and Local File documentation. Even below the threshold, all non-arm's length transactions must be reported on Form T106 (or TP-1068 for Quebec) and reflect arm's length pricing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Quebec do not enforce a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) regime; however, the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act and Part X.1 of the Quebec Taxation Act requires that transactions have a real economic purpose and are not arranged primarily to obtain a tax benefit. For the Quebec LP, the partnership must have substantive commercial activities (warehousing, inventory management, order fulfilment, customer service) and the subscribed capital of limited partners must be actually paid in and at risk; otherwise, deductions and losses may be denied under at-risk rules (s. 96(2.1) and s. 143.2), and a corporate general partner may be treated as a shell if it lacks real control and assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a T5013 or TP-600 that omits Canadian-source subscription box revenues, fabricates expenses, or allocates income to a non-resident partner in a sham arrangement to avoid Quebec income tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty equal to 50% (increased to 100% for false statements made on returns filed after April 1, 2024) of the tax sought to be evaded; criminal prosecution under section 239 of the Income Tax Act and section 49 of the Quebec Tax Administration Act carries fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners are jointly and severally liable for the partnership's tax debts; a limited partner who participates in management loses limited liability; directors or officers of a corporate general partner may be liable for unremitted source deductions (CPP, EI, GST/HST, QST) under section 227.1 of the ITA and may face travel bans, asset freezes, or civil restitution orders under section 160

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance (GAAR and Treaty Shopping)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the LP as a mailbox entity with no Quebec plant, employees, or physical inventory; all subscription-box operational decisions are made outside Canada; the LP merely holds invoices and routes profits to non-resident partners to exploit treaty rates without any real risk or management
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under GAAR denying the intended tax benefit; transfer pricing penalties of 10% on the net transfer pricing adjustment if the adjustment exceeds CAD 5,000 and no reasonable efforts are documented; loss of limited liability protection under Quebec civil law for partners who exercise control; Quebec Registraire des entreprises can also strike the LP off the registry for non-compliance with the shareholder transparency register requirements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate general partner and its directors may be held liable under asset-transference rules (section 160 ITA) for tax owed by the partnership if assets were transferred to a non-resident for less than fair value; a director with significant outstanding tax debt may be barred from travel by the CRA under the Tax Collection Rules, and the Quebec Minister of Revenue can issue a restriction certificate preventing the director from selling, leasing, or purchasing certain assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing with Foreign Affiliates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing subscription-box product sales to a foreign related distributor or paying inflated royalties to an offshore related IP owner for the subscription-box trademark and branding, without executing arm's length agreements or contemporaneous documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment plus a penalty of 10% of the total net adjustment under section 247(3) of the Income Tax Act when the adjustment exceeds the lesser of CAD 5,000 or 10% of the taxpayer's gross revenue; interest is charged on deficiencies; Revenu Québec may apply a parallel penalty under section 48.0.1 of the Tax Administration Act and disallow the deferral or deduction entirely if the arrangement is artificial
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner (or director of the corporate general partner) is jointly and severally liable for the transfer pricing penalty and interest; if the general partner is a non-resident shell, its directors can be served under Canadian cross-border business standards and may face seizure of Canadian assets, garnishment of subscription box receivables, and personal liability to the extent of distributions received from the LP during insolvency

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership / Registraire des Entreprises Non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain the Quebec register of individuals with significant control (Registre des personnes moralement ou réellement titulaires), failing to disclose the ultimate limited partners, or ignoring know-your-client (KYC) procedures for high-volume subscription payment chargebacks, refunds, and bounced payments, creating a channel for money laundering through packaged goods
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Quebec's Act to Improve Corporate Transparency (2019), an LP can be administratively dissolved or struck off for failing to provide beneficial ownership information; administrative fines up to CAD 100,000 for individuals and CAD 500,000 for corporations; under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, penalties for failing to implement an AML compliance program can reach CAD 1,000,000 for a corporate entity and CAD 500,000 for individuals
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners of the LP can be personally prohibited from serving on any Quebec board for up to five years, and the registraire may impose personal fines; CRA and Revenu Québec can pursue the directors personally for unpaid GST/QST and income tax amounts if the corporate general partner is deemed to be a nominee, effectively piercing the corporate veil; serious AML violations may lead to a personal criminal record, imprisonment, and, where assets in Canada are held through the LP, provisional freezing orders restricting the director's bank accounts
